Greatest Olympiad Underdogs - The Underdog
rubriker._rss_content: In this Olympiad special of The Underdog, Robert Ris presents seven remarkable upsets from both the Women’s and Open sections, chosen not only for the rating differences but also for the instructive chess behind them. The examples range from spectacular attacking ideas and sudden tactical reversals to missed winning chances and difficult endgames, showing how quickly a game can turn even when the stronger player appears to be completely in control. One particularly dramatic example sees Arjun Erigaisi lose after dominating much of his game, while another features a rating difference of almost 600 points and a winning material advantage that disappears after a major tactical oversight.

rubriker.title: Turlov: Chess is massively undervalued
rubriker._rss_content: He has been elected FIDE President. Shortly before the ballot decided it in Samarkand, American Chess Magazine conducted an interview with Timur Turlov, discussing his upbringing and background, the ecosystem of his company Freedom, his involvement in chess and what he would do to enhance its popularity and status in the world. Long, must-read description.

rubriker.title: «El viaje de la dama», nueva obra de Soppe y Carranza
rubriker._rss_content: «El viaje de la dama», de Guillermo Gustavo Soppe y Juan Carlos Carranza, recorre la transformación histórica y simbólica de la pieza más poderosa del ajedrez, combinando divulgación, análisis técnico y reflexión cultural. La obra dedica además un espacio central a la historia del ajedrez femenino, con especial atención a figuras argentinas como Edith Soppe, Claudia Amura, Liliana Burijovich, Sandra Villegas y Candela Francisco. | Imágenes: Cortesía de los autores
